Root owns separate _totalAssets, ERC20 share supply, pending/claimable controller balances and redemption queue. Distinct financial accounting/issuer product using Accountable infrastructure, not a mere curator alias. Travessia does not claim authorship of Accountable shared source.
sourceSemantics.funding: deposit/mint check controller caller/already-operator, hook strategy to enforce capacity/minimum/loan state, mint recipient TTV and pull controller AUSD into accounted vault assets. Standard two-arg variants set controller=caller.
sourceSemantics.permission: PermissionLevel.None(0) observed at pinned block: no new signature data or auth signing is needed for canonical plain financial calldata. setOperator, setSigner and setAllowed excluded.
sourceSemantics.recipientOwnership: requestRedeem separately checks owner caller/already-operator and controller caller/already-operator, then escrows shares and updates controller. redeem/withdraw require controller authority and claimable bounds. cancel returns pending escrow to chosen receiver under controller authority.
sourceSemantics.rounding: deposit floors shares; mint ceils assets. redeem floors payout but uses ceil assets to conservatively debit claimable balance. withdraw burns floor shares while ceiled shares decrement controller claimable ledger; rounding differs from ordinary ERC4626 assumptions.
sourceSemantics.risk: Interest-accrued sharePrice and any default/loss/fees originate in upgradeable dedicated strategy, not token balance alone; assets may leave on-chain custody for trade loans. Future repayment, legal recoverability and early exit availability not assured.

Travessia Credit

Overview

Travessia Credit is an on-chain credit protocol that uses programmable infrastructure to finance real-world trade finance operations.

Users deposit stablecoins into smart contract vaults that deploy capital into short-duration credit loans. In return, users earn yield generated by real-world economic activity from operators on the Travessia platform.

Travessia gives real businesses access to scalable working capital and gives vault users exposure to predictable, short-duration, and uncorrelated credit.

Why Travessia Exists

Trade is one of the largest and most important parts of the global economy. Goods move between producers, suppliers, logistics providers, buyers, and end customers every day. But trade does not move by itself. It needs financing.

Before a product is delivered and paid for, someone has to provide working capital. Producers need to be paid. Goods need to be sourced. Logistics need to be arranged. Invoices need to be issued. Buyers often pay only after delivery. That timing gap is what trade finance exists to solve.

Trade finance provides capital between the moment a seller needs to produce, purchase, or deliver goods and the moment the buyer pays. In its simplest form, trade finance bridges the gap between production, delivery, invoicing, and payment.

Despite its importance, trade finance is still difficult to access and scale. Strong local operators have real trade flows but limited access to global capital. Global investors want access to short-duration private credit but lack the local infrastructure, reporting, legal structure, and monitoring needed to underwrite these transactions directly.

Travessia exists to align these two sides. We are building the infrastructure that makes global trade finance investable at scale.

Security, Audits, and Risk Controls

Travessia is designed with the assumption that trust must be earned through structure, transparency, and verification rather than reputation or promises.

This section outlines how the protocol approaches security, auditing, and risk management across both on-chain and real-world components.

Smart Contract Security

All core protocol logic is implemented through smart contracts that govern capital movement, yield accrual, settlement timing, and withdrawals.

Contracts are designed to:

  • enforce fixed deployment rules
  • remove discretionary control over user funds
  • ensure predictable capital behavior across cycles and epochs
  • clearly separate protocol enforcement from real-world execution

Critical parameters such as deployment timing, accrual windows, and settlement requirements are enforced on chain and cannot be modified arbitrarily.

Independent Audits

Smart contracts used by Travessia’s smart contracts have been audited by independent third-party security firms.

Operational Risk and Real-World Execution

Travessia does not rely on on-chain activity alone to generate returns. Capital is deployed into real-world operations executed by professional counterparties.

Operational risk is managed through:

  • short deployment cycles
  • continuous capital rotation
  • disciplined settlement timelines
  • limited exposure windows per transaction
  • predefined return obligations to the protocol

The protocol does not warehouse inventory, extend long-term credit, or take directional exposure to commodity prices.

Hedging and Market Risk Management

To mitigate price volatility during execution, operators employ hedging strategies using established futures markets.

Hedging is used to:

  • protect margins between purchase and sale
  • reduce exposure to short-term price fluctuations
  • align execution outcomes with fixed settlement cycles

Hedging is not used to increase leverage or amplify returns.

Transparency Through Verified Data

Travessia is building a real-time transparency dashboard that provides visibility into underlying economic activity.

This dashboard will surface:

  • execution data supplied directly by Brazilian government sources
  • transaction attestations tied to real-world activity
  • aggregate volume, settlement, and throughput metrics
  • protocol-level performance indicators

All data displayed will be verified and sourced from official public records rather than self-reported metrics.

This system adds an additional layer of transparency and risk control by allowing users and investors to independently observe the economic activity supporting protocol returns.

Separation of Duties and Controls

Travessia is structured so that:

  • smart contracts control capital rules
  • operators execute real-world activity
  • no single party can unilaterally change system behavior

Operators cannot:

  • modify accrual rules
  • extend settlement windows
  • delay capital return
  • alter withdrawal mechanics

Likewise, protocol governance cannot directly execute real-world operations.

This separation reduces both technical and operational risk.

Liquidity and Redemption Risk

In Version One, liquidity is governed by cycle boundaries and settlement windows. Early exits are allowed but priced explicitly to reflect real-world unwind costs.

In Version Two, liquidity is provided through secondary markets for vault receipt tokens. Pricing reflects time remaining in active epochs, fees, and available liquidity rather than artificial guarantees.

This approach ensures that liquidity risk is surfaced transparently rather than hidden within protocol assumptions.

Known Risks and Disclosures

As with any system bridging on-chain and real-world activity, risks exist.

These include, but are not limited to:

  • smart contract vulnerabilities
  • operational execution risk
  • FX and settlement risk
  • counterparty risk
  • regulatory uncertainty
  • liquidity variability during early stages

Travessia’s approach is to acknowledge these risks explicitly, structure the system to minimize them, and provide transparency so participants can make informed decisions.

Ongoing Improvements

Security and transparency are not static.

Travessia intends to:

  • publish ongoing audit updates
  • expand transparency dashboards as data availability increases
  • improve monitoring and alerting systems
  • iterate on risk controls as the protocol scales

These improvements are expected to evolve alongside product versions and additional vault deployments.

Summary

Travessia’s security model is built on three pillars:

  • deterministic on-chain enforcement
  • disciplined real-world execution
  • verifiable transparency

Together, these elements provide the foundation required to generate large, repeatable, and uncorrelated returns rooted in essential industries.

Frequently Asked Questions

About Travessia Credit

What is Travessia Credit in one sentence?

Travessia Credit is an on-chain credit protocol that routes stablecoin capital into real-world operations in essential industries to generate verifiable, uncorrelated returns.

How long has Travessia been operating?

Travessia is a newly launched protocol, but the underlying economic activity and operators it supports have existed and operated for years prior to the protocol’s launch.

Is Travessia a lender or an investment fund?

Neither. Travessia provides programmable credit infrastructure. It does not make discretionary lending decisions or manage capital as a fund.

Returns and Economics

Where do returns come from?

Returns are generated by real-world transaction execution in essential industries. They come from operational margins and capital turnover, not from token incentives or market appreciation.

Are returns correlated to crypto markets?

Returns are designed to be uncorrelated. They depend on real-world transaction volume and settlement activity rather than token prices or market direction.

Are returns fixed or variable?

Returns are fixed for each deployment cycle and accrue continuously while capital is active. Rates may vary across cycles based on market conditions and execution outcomes.

Capital and Risk

What happens to my capital once I deposit?

Capital is deployed according to predefined rules into real-world operations executed by professional counterparties. Movement, timing, and settlement are enforced by smart contracts.

Is my capital ever traded, leveraged, or rehypothecated?

No. Capital is not traded or leveraged. It is deployed directly into transaction flows and returned on a fixed schedule.

What are the primary risks?

Risks include smart contract vulnerabilities, operational execution risk, FX and settlement risk, counterparty risk, and liquidity variability, particularly in early stages.

Withdrawals and Liquidity

When can I withdraw my funds?

In Version One, full withdrawals are available at the end of each deployment cycle. Early withdrawals are permitted during a cycle subject to penalties and settlement windows.

Can I exit early if I need liquidity?

Yes. Early withdrawals are allowed but incur a penalty and may take up to fourteen days to settle, reflecting real-world unwind costs.

Will instant withdrawals be supported?

Version Two introduces instant exit paths through secondary market trading of vault receipt tokens. Liquidity will be market-driven and scale gradually.

Security and Transparency

Has the protocol been audited?

Smart contracts are undergoing independent third-party audits. Audit reports will be published once completed.

How can I verify what is happening off chain?

Travessia is building a transparency dashboard powered by data verified and supplied directly by Brazilian government sources, providing visibility into underlying economic activity.

Who controls the smart contracts?

Smart contract logic enforces core system behavior. Governance cannot arbitrarily alter capital movement or settlement rules.

The Tauri Vault

Who is Tauri?

Tauri is a Brazilian grain operator executing short-duration spot transactions in one of the world’s largest agricultural markets.

Why is grain the first market?

Grain is essential, high-volume, capital-intensive, and operates on predictable settlement cycles, making it well-suited for programmable credit.

Will Travessia support other industries?

Yes. The protocol is designed to support additional vaults tied to other operators and essential industries over time.

Tokens and Governance

Is there a token?

Travessia plans to introduce a governance token. Details will be published separately once finalized.

What will the token be used for?

The token is intended for governance and protocol alignment. It does not represent equity or ownership of underlying assets.

Participation

Who is Travessia designed for?

Travessia is designed for users and investors seeking exposure to real-world yield that is transparent, disciplined, and uncorrelated with crypto markets.

Is Travessia permissionless?

Participation parameters may vary by vault and jurisdiction. Details will be disclosed per product.

 function convertToAssets(uint256 shares) public view returns (uint256) {\\n        return _convertToAssets(shares, sharePrice(), Math.Rounding.Floor);\\n    }\\n\\n    \/\/\/ @inheritdoc \/\/\/ @dev Computes the assets based on shares and price\\n    function _convertToAssets(uint256 shares, uint256 price, Math.Rounding rounding)\\n        internal\\n        view\\n        virtual\\n uint256 sharesUp = _convertToShares(assets, withdrawPrice, Math.Rounding.Ceil);\\n\\n        strategy.onWithdraw(address(this), assets, receiver, controller);\\n\\n    _requireLoanTermsNotSet();\\n\\n        if (borrower == address(0)) revert ZeroAddress();\\n        if (terms.interestInterval == 0) revert InvalidIntervalLength();\\n        if (terms.withdrawalPeriod \u003e= terms.interestInterval) revert InvalidWithdrawalPeriod();\\n\\n        terms.duration = 0;\\n        _setTerms(terms);\\n\\n        _scaleFactor = PRECISION;\\n\\n        loanState = LoanState.TermsSet;\\n        _loan.termsSetTime = block.timestamp;\\n\\n        emit LoanTermsSet(\\n            terms.minCapacity,\\n            terms.maxCapacity,\\n            terms.interestRate,\\n            terms.lateInterestPenalty,\\n            terms.interestInterval,\\n            terms.duration\\n        );\\n    }\\n\\n    \/\/\/ @inheritdoc IAccountableLoan\\n       terms.duration\\n        );\\n    }\\n\\n    \/\/\/ @inheritdoc IAccountableOpenTerm\\n    function acceptTerms() external nonReentrant onlyBorrower whenNotPaused {\\n        if (loanState == LoanState.TermsSet) {\\n            loanState = LoanState.OngoingDynamic;\\n\\n            _accruedAt = block.timestamp + _loan.depositPeriod;\\n            _loan.startTime = block.timestamp;\\n            _lastPaidTime = block.timestamp;\\n\\n            emit TermsAccepted();\\n            return;\\n        }\\n\\n        _accrueInterest();\\n        _processAvailableWithdrawals();\\n\\n        LoanTerms memory terms = _pendingTerms;\\n        delete _pendingTerms;\\n\\n        uint256 currentMaxCap = _loan.maxCapacity;\\n        if (currentMaxCap \u003e terms.maxCapacity) {\\n            uint256 diff = currentMaxCap - terms.maxCapacity;\\n            if (diff \u003e maxDeposit(address(0), address(0))) revert CapacityTooLow();\\n        }\\n        if (terms.interestInterval == 0) revert InvalidIntervalLength();\\n        if (terms.withdrawalPeriod \u003e= terms.interestInterval) revert InvalidWithdrawalPeriod();\\n        if (terms.withdrawalPeriod \u003e 0 \u0026\u0026 terms.minDeposit;\\n        _loan.minRedeem = terms.minRedeem;\\n        _loan.maxCapacity = terms.maxCapacity;\\n\\n        _loan.interestRate = terms.interestRate;\\n        _loan.interestInterval = rejectTerms() external onlyBorrower whenNotPaused {\\n        if (loanState == LoanState.TermsSet) {\\n            delete _loan;\\n\\n            loanState = LoanState.Initialized;\\n\\n            emit TermsRejected();\\n            return;\\n        }\\n\\n        delete _pendingTerms;\\n\\n        emit TermsRejected();\\n    }\\n\\n    \/\/\/ @inheritdoc IAccountableStrategy\\n    function _updateDelinquentStatus();\\n        }\\n\\n        emit ReserveThresholdSet(threshold);\\n    }\\n\\n    \/\/\/ @inheritdoc IAccountableOpenTerm\\n    function setProposer(address proposer, bool _loan.interestRate = pendingInterestRate;\\n        delete pendingInterestRate;\\n    }\\n\\n    \/\/ ========================================================================== \/\/\\n    \/\/ scaleFactorSnapshot: _scaleFactor\\n        });\\n\\n        _loan.interestRate = newRate;\\n\\n        _updateDelinquentStatus();\\n\\n        emit RatePublished(msg.sender, oldRate, newRate);\\n    }\\n\\n    \/\/\/ @inheritdoc IAccountableOpenTerm\\n    function rollbackRate() external onlyOperationsAdmin {\\n        _requireLoanOngoing();\\n\\n        DVNRateUpdate memory update = _accruedAt = update.timestamp;\\n        _loan.interestRate = update.previousRate;\\n        _scaleFactor = update.scaleFactorSnapshot;\\n\\n        delete lastRateUpdate;\\n\\n        (uint256 assets) external nonReentrant onlySafetyModuleOrManager {\\n        _requireLoanInDefault();\\n\\n        loanState = LoanState.InDefaultClaims;\\n\\n        IAccountableVault(vault).lockAssets(assets, msg.sender);\\n\\n        _updateDelinquentStatus();\\n\\n        emit DefaultCovered(safetyModule, msg.sender, assets);\\n    }\\n\\n    \/\/\/ @inheritdoc borrowable = _borrowable(msg.sender);\\n        uint256 maxBorrowable = Math.min(borrowable, assets);\\n\\n        if (maxBorrowable == 0) revert InsufficientAmount();\\n\\n        \/\/\/ track net _loan.outstandingPrincipal += maxBorrowable.mulDiv(PRECISION, _scaleFactor, Math.Rounding.Ceil);\\n        IAccountableVault(vault).releaseAssets(maxBorrowable, msg.sender);\\n\\n        _updateDelinquentStatus();\\n\\n        emit Borrowed(msg.sender, maxBorrowable);\\n    }\\n\\n    \/\/\/ @inheritdoc IAccountableLoan\\n    function repay(uint256 assets) external nonReentrant onlyBorrower whenNotPaused {\\n        _requireLoanOngoing();\\n\\n        if (assets == 0) revert InsufficientAmount();\\n\\n        _accrueInterest();\\n\\n        address asset_ = asset;\\n        address vault_ = vault;\\n        address feeManager_ = feeManager;\\n        uint256 scaleFactor_ = _scaleFactor;\\n\\n        uint256 principalShares = _loan.outstandingPrincipal;\\n        uint256 principalAssets = principalShares.mulDiv(scaleFactor_, PRECISION, Math.Rounding.Ceil);\\n\\n        uint256 establishmentFee =\\n            _prorataFee(principalAssets, IFeeManager(feeManager_).establishmentFee(address(this)));\\n        if (establishmentFee \u003e assets) revert InsufficientAmount();\\n\\n        uint256 repaymentPrincipal = Math.min(assets - establishmentFee, principalAssets);\\n        netPrincipal = netPrincipal \u003e= repaymentPrincipal ? netPrincipal - repaymentPrincipal : 0;\\n        IERC20(asset_).safeTransferFrom(msg.sender, 0, 0, establishmentFee);\\n        }\\n\\n        IAccountableVault(vault_).lockAssets(repaymentPrincipal, address(this));\\n\\n        _loan.outstandingPrincipal -= LoanState.Repaid;\\n        }\\n        _updateDelinquentStatus();\\n\\n        emit LoanRepaid(repaymentPrincipal + establishmentFee);\\n    }\\n\\n    \/\/\/ @inheritdoc IAccountableLoan\\n    function prepay() external pure {\\n        revert NotSupportedByStrategy();\\n    }\\n\\n    \/\/\/ @inheritdoc IAccountableLoan\\n    function pay(uint256) external pure {\\n        revert              \/\/\\n    \/\/ ========================================================================== \/\/\\n\\n    \/\/\/ @dev Overridden deposit hook with extra validation logic and balances update\\n    function onDeposit(address share, uint256 assets, address, address)\\n        public\\n        override(AccountableStrategy, IStrategyVaultHooks)\\n        nonReentrant\\n        onlyVault\\n        whenNotPaused\\n        returns (uint256 price)\\n    {\\n        _requireCanDeposit();\\n        _requireMinDepositAmount(assets);\\n\\n        _accrueInterest();\\n\\n        _requireBelowMaxCapacity(assets);\\n\\n        price = _sharePrice(share);\\n    }\\n\\n    \/\/\/ @dev Overridden mint hook with extra validation logic and balances update\\n    function whenNotPaused\\n        returns (uint256 price)\\n    {\\n        _requireCanDeposit();\\n\\n        _accrueInterest();\\n\\n        price = _sharePrice(share);\\n        uint256 assets = _sharePrice(share);\\n\\n        uint256 assets = shares.mulDiv(price, PRECISION);\\n\\n        if (_isInstantRedeem()) {\\n            canFulfill = true;\\n        } else {\\n            uint256 availableLiquidity = _getAvailableLiquidity();\\n            if (availableLiquidity \u003e= assets) {\\n                canFulfill = true;\\n            } else if (_loan.withdrawalPeriod != 0) {\\n                _createOrAddWithdrawalBatch(shares, controller);\\n                canFulfill = false;\\n            }\\n        }\\n    }\\n\\n    \/\/\/ @dev Overridden onCancelRedeemRequest hook for updating batches upon cancellation\\n    function onCancelRedeemRequest(address share, address controller)\\n        public\\n        override(AccountableStrategy, IStrategyVaultHooks)\\n        nonReentrant\\n        onlyVault\\n        whenNotPaused\\n        returns (bool canCancel)\\n    {\\n        \/\/ 0 id since state is controller based and the queue id does not change result\\n        uint256 pending = IAccountableAsyncRedeemVault(share).pendingRedeemRequest(0, controller);\\n\\n        uint256 tracked;\\n        for (uint256 batch = pendingBatch; batch \u003c= currentBatch;) {\\n            tracked += _controllerBatchShares[controller][batch];\\n            unchecked {\\n                ++batch;\\n            }\\n        }\\n\\n        uint256 processed = tracked \u003e pending ? tracked - pending : 0;\\n\\n        for (uint256 batch = pendingBatch; batch \u003c= currentBatch;) {\\n            uint256 allocated = _controllerBatchShares[controller][batch];\\n\\n            if (allocated \u003e 0) {\\n                if (processed \u003e 0) {\\n                    uint256 amountProcessed = Math.min(processed, allocated);\\n                    allocated -= amountProcessed;\\n                    processed -= amountProcessed;\\n                }\\n\\n                if (allocated \u003e 0) {\\n                    _withdrawalBatches[batch].totalShares -= allocated;\\n                }\\n\\n                delete _controllerBatchShares[controller][batch];\\n            }\\n            unchecked {\\n                ++batch;\\n            }\\n        }\\n\\n        return true;\\n    }\\n\\n    function onFeeStructureChange() public override(AccountableStrategy, IFeeManagerHooks) nonReentrant {\\n        super.onFeeStructureChange();\\n        if (loanState == LoanState.OngoingDynamic) {\\n            _accrueInterest();\\n        }\\n    }\\n\\n    \/\/\/ @dev Overridden maxDeposit hook\\n    \/\/\/ @dev Uses virtual accrual to return accurate capacity based on current timestamp\\n    function maxDeposit(address, address)\\n        public\\n        view\\n        override(AccountableStrategy, IStrategyVaultHooks)\\n        returns (uint256 maxAssets)\\n    {\\n        uint256 netPrincipal_ = netPrincipal;\\n        uint256 maxCapacity_ = _loan.maxCapacity;\\n        uint256 totalAssets = IAccountableVault(vault).totalAssets();\\n        uint256 capMinusDebt = maxCapacity_ \u003e netPrincipal_ ? maxCapacity_ - netPrincipal_ : 0;\\n        maxAssets = totalAssets \u003e= capMinusDebt ? 0 : capMinusDebt - totalAssets;\\n    }\\n\\n
